cohort: 235 women with severe preeclampsia and 470 women without severe preeclampsia
finding: The study identified several risk factors for severe preeclampsia, including maternal age > 35 years, gestational or chronic hypertension, obesity, use of assisted reproduction, prior preeclampsia, and chronic kidney disease, and found that severe preeclampsia was associated with higher rates of cesarean section, prematurity, and perinatal mortality
mod_finding: Cesarean section rate was higher in the severe preeclampsia group compared to the control group (60% vs. 20.9%, p < 0.001).
